From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC Plan & Success Criteria — next steps

Hi Katie / Peter —

Thanks again for the call today — good to align on goals and scope. Per our conversation, I captured a proposed POC plan and success criteria below. Attaching the full POC plan for reference (redwood-poc-plan.pdf).

Quick recap / proposed success criteria (please confirm or edit):
- Latency: p95 model-response latency <= 250ms (server-side, excluding client network).
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/sec with 99% success under baseline workload (target can scale to 100 RPS if we provide extra capacity).
- Cost: effective cost/token <= $0.0008 at POC volume (include quantized model variants where applicable).
- Quality: pass-rate on your evaluation prompt set >= 92% (we'll use the 10k prompt sample you mentioned + a separate holdout set of 1k prompts).
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate, end-to-end SLA for availability during test windows.

Proposed timeline (4-week POC):
- Week 0 (ASAP): SOW & S3 access + account setup + signoff on success criteria.
- Week 1: Integration & baseline measurements (instrumentation, test harness, sample runs).
- Week 2: Load + throughput tuning; iterate on batching/quantization settings.
- Week 3: Quality evaluation & fixes (prompt engineering, model variants).
- Week 4: Final evaluation, findings, and recommended next steps (Dedicated/Private options).

Owners:
- Jordan Blake (sales): timeline, exec updates, commercial paperwork.
- Lauren Bishop (SE): environment setup, test harness, metrics collection.
- Marcus Lin (Customer Success): runbook, monitoring, ops support during test windows.

Immediate next steps for Acme:
1) Confirm the success criteria above (latency, throughput, cost, quality).
2) Share the 10k sample prompt set and sample traffic profile (S3 link preferred).
3) Sign the attached SOW so we can schedule an integration window (we can start Week 1 as soon as SOW is signed and we have credentials).

I'll follow up with a short SOW/statement of work and proposed test windows — Lauren, Marcus: looping you for visibility and to call out any immediate blockers.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake

Thanks Jordan — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications / asks from our side:

- The 10k prompt sample: we will share a sanitized S3 bucket by EOD Monday. The dataset includes a 1k holdout set for final scoring.
- Quality metric: when you say "pass-rate >= 92%", can you propose the exact scoring rubric? We prefer deterministic scoring for the first pass (string match + normalized tokens) and a small human review for edge cases.
- Cost: can you provide a rough cost projection for the 4-week run (including any burst capacity) so we can budget?

Also, we'd like to include our infra lead (Peter) in the integration planning — he will review any network/firewall requirements.

If the success criteria above are acceptable, we can sign the SOW this week.

Thanks,

Hi Katie / Peter —

Thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the dataset share. Below are a few clarifications and an ask on cost projection so we can lock the SOW this week. I've attached a draft SLA and SOW language (sla-draft.docx) for review.

Scoring rubric (proposed):
- Automated scoring: token-normalized exact match + fuzzy string match threshold for ranking tasks. We'll run the 10k sample through the harness and compute pass/fail per item.
- Human review: sample 200 failure cases for qualitative triage; we report precision/recall-style metrics and root cause categories.
- Final quality pass if automated pass-rate >= 92% AND human-verified false-positive rate <= 5%.

Metric details (to be instrumented in the test harness):
- Latency p95: measure server-side request-to-last-token-emitted (exclude client network). Target <= 250ms.
- Throughput: measure sustained RPS and tail latency under load. Baseline target 50 RPS; stretch target 100 RPS.
- Cost/token: compute end-to-end cost per token using our billing estimator (we'll provide a rough projection).
- Errors: 5xx and model-failure rates to be <= 1%.

Ownership & immediate actions:
- Jordan Blake: finalize SOW + commercial signoff. (Action: send SOW link & target sign date by Tue 3/17).
- Lauren Bishop: create test harness repo and example client; outline required infra (S3, service account, ephemeral API keys). (Action: initial PR with test harness by Wed 3/18).
- Marcus Lin: define monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds; provide playbook for remediation during load tests. (Action: dashboard links + runbook by Thu 3/19).

Request for Acme:
1) Please confirm the scoring rubric above or suggest edits.
2) Grant Redwood a sanitized S3 read-only bucket for the 10k prompts and a way to push logs/results back to your team.
3) Any firewall/VPC constraints — Peter, please share the required IP allowlist or proxy details.

Cost projection: Lauren and I will produce a preliminary cost estimate once we know the expected test duration and concurrency. Expect a one-page estimate within 24 hours after S3 access is provided.

If this looks good, we can lock a kickoff slot next week and kick off Week 1 integration.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC Plan & Success Criteria — quick technical notes

Quick internal notes after reading the thread / plan:

- Test harness: I'll base the repo on the standard Redwood POC harness (instrumented with p95/p99 timers and per-request token accounting). I'll include example load scripts (wrk-like) and a small driver that replays the 10k prompts deterministically.
- Quantization/batching: to hit the latency target at 50 RPS we'll likely use int8 quantization + dynamic batching with a max batch size of 8; for the 100 RPS stretch we should evaluate kernel-level optimizations and possibly the 4-GPU shard config.
- Metrics: confirm that latency p95 excludes client-side overhead. We'll emit the following fields: request_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, batch_size, error_code.
- Security: Acme will need ephemeral API keys and a short-lived role; we should not request long-lived credentials. Marcus, can you draft the ephemeral key flow?

I'll start the test-harness PR tomorrow and include run instructions. If Peter needs any specific IP ranges, let me know and I'll get the infra notes ready.

— Lauren
